headline: Tough Super Bowl comp and investment swing overshadow margin
summary_short: Fox's quarter ended March 31, 2026 revenue fell to $3,994M (-8.6% y/y) on the absence of Super Bowl LIX advertising, and diluted EPS dropped to $0.38 (-49.3% y/y) mainly on a $499M non-operating fair-value swing, even as segment Adjusted EBITDA rose 11% y/y to $954M.
summary_long: Revenue of $3,994M fell 8.6% y/y and 22.9% q/q as a $480M/24% drop in advertising revenue — tied to the absent Super Bowl LIX broadcast and lower ratings, partly offset by Tubi AVOD growth and an extra NFL game — outweighed higher distribution and content revenue. Segment Adjusted EBITDA still rose 11% y/y to $954M on lower sports-rights amortization. GAAP net income fell 52% y/y to $166M (diluted EPS $0.38, -49.3%) almost entirely due to a $499M non-operating swing in equity-securities fair value, not operations. Cash fell to $3,601M from $4,815M a year ago after $1.9B of buybacks and $275M of dividends YTD; long-term debt eased to $6,605M. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Results were dominated by a swing in the fair value of equity-securities investments and the loss of Super Bowl LIX advertising versus the prior-year quarter, only partly offset by higher segment profitability and digital growth.

Advertising revenue fell $480M/24% on the absence of the February 2025 Super Bowl LIX broadcast and lower ratings, only partly offset by Tubi AVOD digital growth, an extra NFL postseason game, and higher distribution rates per subscriber.

Operating expenses fell $471M/16%, primarily on lower sports-programming rights amortization tied to the absent Super Bowl broadcast, partially offset by Fox One launch costs and higher entertainment programming costs.
Net income fell mainly because of a swing in fair value on the Company's equity-securities investments, partly offset by higher Segment EBITDA — the release's own stated explanation.

Tracks the same GAAP profit swing as net income: a $499M non-operating fair-value loss on equity investments hit pretax income even though segment-level Adjusted EBITDA (which excludes that item) rose 11% y/y.
Mirrors the EBIT move above; the GAAP-basis figure absorbs the non-operating investment loss that the Company's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA measure (+11% y/y to $954M) excludes.
Mirrors the Net income decline; weighted-average diluted shares fell to about 432M from 461M a year earlier on buybacks, a modest cushion that only partly offset the profit drop.
Mirrors the Diluted EPS move above, reflecting the same net income decline against a comparably reduced basic share count.
